title: Exodus Chapter 39 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Exodus chapter 39 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Exodus Chapter 39 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Exodus Chapter 39.

questions.question: What colors were used to make the cloths of service and holy garments for Aaron?
questions.correctAnswer: Blue, purple, and scarlet
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:1 states that blue, purple, and scarlet were used to make the cloths of service and holy garments for Aaron.

questions.question: What materials were used to make the ephod according to Exodus 39?
options: Gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen
questions.correctAnswer: Gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:2 states that the ephod was made of gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen.

questions.question: How was the gold prepared for working into the ephod?
options: Beaten into thin plates and cut into wires
questions.correctAnswer: Beaten into thin plates and cut into wires
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:3 describes that the gold was beaten into thin plates and cut into wires to work it into the blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen.

questions.question: What was made to couple the two edges of the ephod together?
questions.correctAnswer: Shoulderpieces
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:4 explains that shoulderpieces were made to couple the two edges of the ephod together.

questions.question: The curious girdle of the ephod was made of which materials?
options: Gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen
questions.correctAnswer: Gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:5 specifies the curious girdle was made of gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen according to the work of the ephod.

questions.question: What stones were engraved with the names of the children of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Onyx stones
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:6 states that onyx stones were graven, as signets are graven, with the names of the children of Israel.

questions.question: Where were the onyx stones set on the ephod?
options: On the shoulders of the ephod
On the hem of the garment
questions.correctAnswer: On the shoulders of the ephod
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:7 says the onyx stones were put on the shoulders of the ephod as a memorial to the children of Israel.

questions.question: What materials were used to make the breastplate?
options: Gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen
questions.correctAnswer: Gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:8 states the breastplate was made of gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen, like the ephod.

questions.question: What was the shape and size of the breastplate?
options: Foursquare and double, a span in length and breadth
Circular and flat, a cubit in diameter
Rectangular and single, two spans long
questions.correctAnswer: Foursquare and double, a span in length and breadth
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:9 describes the breastplate as foursquare, double, with length and breadth each a span.

questions.question: Which stones were in the first row of the breastplate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sardius, topaz, and carbuncle
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:10 states the first row of stones in the breastplate was sardius, topaz, and carbuncle.

questions.question: True or False: The stones on the breastplate were engraved with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:14 says the stones were according to the names of the children of Israel, like engravings of a signet, each with the name of one of the twelve tribes.

questions.question: True or False: The breastplate had chains made of silver to fasten it.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:15 states the chains at the ends of the breastplate were made of wreathen work of pure gold, not silver.

questions.question: True or False: The gold used in the ephod was beaten into thin plates and cut into wires for working into the fabric.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:3 describes that gold was beaten into thin plates and cut into wires to be worked into the blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen.

questions.question: True or False: The shoulderpieces were made to couple the two edges of the ephod together.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:4 states that shoulderpieces were made to couple the two edges of the ephod together.

questions.question: In Exodus 39, which instruction comes first?
options: Making the cloths of service of blue, purple, and scarlet
Making the onyx stones engraved with Israel's names
Making the golden girdle of the ephod
questions.correctAnswer: Making the cloths of service of blue, purple, and scarlet
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:1 describes the making of the cloths of service and holy garments first, before instructions about the breastplate and other items.

medium.title: Exodus Chapter 39 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Exodus Chapter 39 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What materials were used to make the two ouches and two gold rings for the breastplate?
questions.correctAnswer: Gold
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:16 states that two ouches of gold and two gold rings were made for the breastplate, emphasizing the use of gold as the sacred material.

questions.question: How were the two wreathen chains connected to the breastplate according to Exodus 39?
options: Put in the two rings on the ends of the breastplate
questions.correctAnswer: Put in the two rings on the ends of the breastplate
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:17 describes that the two wreathen chains of gold were put in the two rings on the ends of the breastplate, indicating a secure and functional connection.

questions.question: Where were the two ends of the wreathen chains fastened?
options: On the shoulderpieces of the ephod
On the bottom of the robe
questions.correctAnswer: On the shoulderpieces of the ephod
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:18 explains that the ends of the wreathen chains were fastened in the two ouches and placed on the shoulderpieces of the ephod, showing how the breastplate was secured.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the two rings placed on the two ends of the breastplate on its inward side?
options: To bind the breastplate to the ephod
To hold the stones in place
To attach the breastplate to Aaron's robe
questions.correctAnswer: To bind the breastplate to the ephod
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:19 indicates that two rings of gold were put on the inward border of the breastplate to facilitate binding it to the ephod, ensuring it stayed securely in place.

questions.question: Where were the other two golden rings placed on the ephod?
options: On the two sides underneath, toward the forepart of it
On the back of the ephod
On the hem of the robe
questions.correctAnswer: On the two sides underneath, toward the forepart of it
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:20 states the two other golden rings were placed on the two sides of the ephod underneath, toward the forepart, showing how the ephod was constructed with multiple rings to secure attachments.

questions.question: According to Exodus 39:21, what was used to bind the breastplate to the ephod and what was the purpose of this binding?
options: A lace of blue; to keep the breastplate above the girdle and prevent it from loosening
A leather strap; to secure the stones firmly
A silver chain; to decorate the ephod
A golden cord; to make the breastplate heavier
questions.correctAnswer: A lace of blue; to keep the breastplate above the girdle and prevent it from loosening
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:21 explains the breastplate was bound by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue to keep it above the girdle and ensure it would not be loosed, highlighting careful adherence to God's command.

questions.question: What was unique about the robe of the ephod in Exodus 39:22 and how does this reflect biblical teaching on holiness?
options: It was made entirely of blue woven work; symbolizing purity and dedication to God's service
It was made of scarlet only; symbolizing sacrifice
It was made of mixed colors; symbolizing diversity
It was made of animal skins; symbolizing protection
questions.correctAnswer: It was made entirely of blue woven work; symbolizing purity and dedication to God's service
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:22 states the robe was all of blue woven work. Blue often symbolizes holiness and heavenly authority, teaching us to be dedicated and pure in our service to God.

questions.question: What feature in the midst of the ephod's robe was designed to prevent tearing, and what might this teach about careful obedience?
options: A band round about the hole; showing the importance of careful craftsmanship and obedience
A hidden seam; protecting the garment
questions.correctAnswer: A band round about the hole; showing the importance of careful craftsmanship and obedience
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:23 describes a hole in the midst of the robe like that of a habergeon, with a band round about it so it would not rend, demonstrating the detailed care and obedience required in preparing holy garments.

questions.question: What alternated around the hem of the robe and what does this combination symbolize in relation to worship?
options: Bells and pomegranates; symbolizing joy and fruitfulness in ministry
Gold and silver beads; signifying wealth
Stars and moons; representing celestial bodies
questions.correctAnswer: Bells and pomegranates; symbolizing joy and fruitfulness in ministry
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:24-26 explain that bells and pomegranates were made upon the hems of the robe, alternating around it, symbolizing joyful service and the fruitfulness expected in the ministry.

questions.question: What garments besides the ephod's robe were made for Aaron and his sons?
options: Coats of fine linen, mitre, bonnets, linen breeches, and a girdle
Robes of scarlet and purple only
questions.correctAnswer: Coats of fine linen, mitre, bonnets, linen breeches, and a girdle
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:27-29 list several garments made for Aaron and his sons including coats of fine linen, mitres, bonnets, linen breeches, and a needleworked girdle, demonstrating thorough preparation for priestly service.

questions.question: What inscription was written on the plate of the holy crown and what does it teach about the attitude toward the Lord?
options: "HOLINESS TO THE LORD"; teaching dedication and reverence
questions.correctAnswer: "HOLINESS TO THE LORD"; teaching dedication and reverence
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:30 reveals the plate of the holy crown was inscribed with "HOLINESS TO THE LORD," teaching that the priest’s work must be dedicated and reverent toward God.

questions.question: What does the binding of the plate to the mitre with a lace of blue symbolize in terms of obedience and faith?
options: Faithful adherence to God's instructions and visible holiness
questions.correctAnswer: Faithful adherence to God's instructions and visible holiness
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:31 shows the plate was tied with a lace of blue to fasten it on the mitre as the LORD commanded Moses, symbolizing faithful obedience and the visible nature of holiness in service.

questions.question: According to Exodus 39:21, what does the passage teach us about the importance of securing our spiritual responsibilities?
options: We must firmly bind our duties so they are not loosened, reflecting steadfastness in faith
We should be flexible and casual about duties
questions.correctAnswer: We must firmly bind our duties so they are not loosened, reflecting steadfastness in faith
questions.explanation: The binding of the breastplate to the ephod with a lace of blue to prevent it from being loosed in Exodus 39:21 teaches the value of steadfastness and careful attention in spiritual responsibilities.

questions.question: True or False: The rings on the breastplate were placed only on the outside of the ephod.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:19 specifies that the rings were put on the inward side of the ephod, showing that the breastplate's attachment was internal and secure, not only external.

questions.question: True or False: The bells and pomegranates on the hem of the robe served a functional purpose in the priest’s ministry.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:25-26 explains that the bells and pomegranates were arranged round about the hem of the robe to minister in, indicating their practical and symbolic role in worship.

hard.title: Exodus Chapter 39 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Exodus Chapter 39.

questions.question: What was tied unto the plate of the holy crown to fasten it on high upon the mitre?
questions.correctAnswer: A lace of blue
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:31 states that they tied unto the plate a lace of blue to fasten it on high upon the mitre, as the LORD commanded Moses.

questions.question: According to Exodus 39, who completed all the work of the tabernacle exactly as the LORD commanded?
questions.correctAnswer: The children of Israel
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:32 and 39:42 affirm that the children of Israel made all the work according to all that the LORD commanded Moses.

questions.question: Which item was NOT mentioned as part of the tabernacle furniture brought to Moses?
questions.correctAnswer: Golden calf
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:33-39 lists furniture items including the ark, altars, and laver but does not mention a golden calf, which appears earlier in Exodus 32.

questions.question: What materials were used to make the covering of the tabernacle according to Exodus 39?
options: Rams' skins dyed red and badgers' skins
questions.correctAnswer: Rams' skins dyed red and badgers' skins
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:34 specifies that the coverings were of rams' skins dyed red and badgers' skins.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the robes worn by Aaron and his sons?
options: Made of fine linen woven work, including coats, mitres, bonnets, breeches and girdles
Made of animal skins with embroidered names of tribes
Made solely from blue and scarlet cloth
Made from gold and silver threads only
questions.correctAnswer: Made of fine linen woven work, including coats, mitres, bonnets, breeches and girdles
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:27-29 describes the holy garments including coats, mitres, bonnets, breeches, and girdles made of fine twined linen and embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet.

questions.question: What phrase was engraved on the plate of the holy crown worn by Aaron?
questions.correctAnswer: "HOLINESS TO THE LORD"
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:30 states that the plate was engraved with the phrase "HOLINESS TO THE LORD".

questions.question: How were the twelve stones on the breastplate arranged and what did they represent?
options: In four rows of three stones representing the twelve tribes of Israel
In a single row representing the twelve apostles
Randomly placed to symbolize divine mystery
Set in a circle representing eternity
questions.correctAnswer: In four rows of three stones representing the twelve tribes of Israel
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:9-14 describe the breastplate as foursquare with four rows of three stones each, representing the names of the twelve tribes of Israel like signet engravings.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Exodus 39 to emphasize the faithful obedience of the Israelites in constructing the tabernacle?
options: Inclusio, framing the chapter with references to the LORD's command and obedience
Chiasm, arranging materials and garments in a mirrored structure
Parallelism, repeating the instructions for the ephod and breastplate
Foreshadowing, hinting at the coming temple in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio, framing the chapter with references to the LORD's command and obedience
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:1 and 39:43 frame the chapter by stating the work was done as the LORD commanded, showing inclusio to emphasize faithful obedience.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of 'HOLINESS TO THE LORD' inscribed on the priestly crown in Exodus 39?
options: Leviticus 8:9, where Aaron is consecrated as priest
questions.correctAnswer: Leviticus 8:9, where Aaron is consecrated as priest
questions.explanation: Leviticus 8:9 describes the high priest wearing the holy crown with the inscription 'HOLINESS TO THE LORD,' connecting directly to Exodus 39:30.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word translated as 'ephod' in Exodus 39, and what was its significance?
options: 'Ephod' means 'to cover' or 'to bind', and it was the sacred priestly garment worn by Aaron
'Ephod' means 'holy place', referring to the tabernacle interior
questions.correctAnswer: 'Ephod' means 'to cover' or 'to bind', and it was the sacred priestly garment worn by Aaron
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root of 'ephod' relates to binding or covering, and Exodus 39:2 describes it as the sacred garment woven with gold and colors, worn by Aaron as high priest.

questions.question: True or False: The bells and pomegranates on the hem of the high priest's robe were made of silver and red cloth.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:24-26 states the pomegranates were made of blue, purple, scarlet, and twined linen, and the bells were made of pure gold, not silver or red cloth.

questions.question: Why did Moses bless the Israelites after examining the completed tabernacle work?
options: Because they had done all the work exactly as the LORD commanded
Because they finished the work ahead of schedule
Because they used only the finest materials
Because they added their own innovations to the design
questions.correctAnswer: Because they had done all the work exactly as the LORD commanded
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:43 states Moses blessed them after seeing that the work was done exactly as the LORD had commanded.

questions.question: Which component of the tabernacle's construction in Exodus 39 foreshadows Christ's role as High Priest?
options: The ephod and breastplate worn by Aaron
The bronze altar used for sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: The ephod and breastplate worn by Aaron
questions.explanation: The ephod and breastplate symbolize the High Priest's intercession and authority, which the New Testament (Hebrews 4:14-16) connects to Christ's priestly role, as introduced in Exodus 39:2-14.

questions.question: Which verse describes the use of 'wreathen work of pure gold' in the priestly garments?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 39:15
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:15 describes the making of chains at the ends of the breastplate of wreathen (twisted) work of pure gold.

questions.question: True or False: The children of Israel only partially followed the LORD's commands in making the tabernacle and its furnishings.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:42 and 39:43 confirm that the children of Israel made all the work exactly according to all the LORD had commanded Moses.

theological.title: Exodus Chapter 39 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Exodus Chapter 39 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does the construction of the ephod with gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen in Exodus 39:2 reveal about God's nature?
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness and majesty
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:2 describes the ephod made with precious materials, symbolizing God's holiness and majestic presence among His people, as these rich colors and gold represent divine glory and sanctity.

questions.question: According to Exodus 39:6-7, what theological significance do the onyx stones engraved with the names of the children of Israel on the ephod's shoulders hold?
options: They symbolize God's remembrance and covenant faithfulness to Israel
They represent human sinfulness carried by the priest
They are merely decorative with no deeper meaning
questions.correctAnswer: They symbolize God's remembrance and covenant faithfulness to Israel
questions.explanation: Verses 6-7 affirm that the onyx stones are a memorial for the children of Israel, indicating God's continual remembrance and faithfulness to His covenant people, a key divine attribute.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about the priestly role is taught by the detailed construction of the breastplate with twelve precious stones each named after the tribes of Israel (Exodus 39:8-14)?
options: The priest represents the entire nation before God
The priest acts independently of Israel
The breastplate is a symbol of earthly power
questions.correctAnswer: The priest represents the entire nation before God
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:8-14 shows that the breastplate with twelve stones representing the tribes indicates the priest's role as mediator, carrying the whole nation before God, reflecting the doctrine of representation in worship.

questions.question: How do the 'chains of pure gold' and the 'gold rings' described in Exodus 39:15-21 contribute to the theological symbolism of the high priest's garments?
options: They signify the unity and inseparability of God's covenant with Israel
They symbolize the priest's personal wealth
They represent the fragility of human worship
They indicate the separation of priest and people
questions.correctAnswer: They signify the unity and inseparability of God's covenant with Israel
questions.explanation: The chains and rings fastening the breastplate to the ephod (Exodus 39:15-21) symbolize the inseparable bond God establishes with His people through covenant, displaying divine faithfulness and unity.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated through the command that the robe be woven all of blue with pomegranates and golden bells on its hem (Exodus 39:22-26)?
questions.correctAnswer: God's glory and divine presence
questions.explanation: The blue robe with pomegranates and golden bells (Exodus 39:22-26) reflects God's glory and presence among His people, as blue often symbolizes heaven and divine majesty in Scripture.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is conveyed by the inscription 'HOLINESS TO THE LORD' on the golden plate of the holy crown in Exodus 39:30?
options: The doctrine of divine holiness and consecration
The doctrine of justification by faith
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine holiness and consecration
questions.explanation: The inscription 'HOLINESS TO THE LORD' (Exodus 39:30) emphasizes God's absolute holiness and the necessity of consecration, reflecting the theological truth of God's separate and pure nature.

questions.question: How does Exodus 39:32-43 demonstrate the attribute of God's faithfulness in relation to His commands?
options: Israel obeyed all God's commands as given through Moses
questions.correctAnswer: Israel obeyed all God's commands as given through Moses
questions.explanation: Verses 32-43 show the Israelites completed all the work exactly as the LORD commanded Moses, demonstrating God's faithfulness in providing clear instructions and Israel's obedience in fulfilling them.

questions.question: What combined teaching about divine provision and human craftsmanship is presented by Exodus 39:3 and 39:29?
options: God provides the materials and commands, while humans execute with skill
God does all work directly without human involvement
Human skill is unnecessary in divine service
The materials are unimportant in worship
questions.correctAnswer: God provides the materials and commands, while humans execute with skill
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:3 describes skilled work with gold and linen, and 39:29 mentions needlework as commanded by God, illustrating divine provision combined with human craftsmanship in worship service.

questions.question: What theological insight about God's covenant relationship with Israel can be drawn from the naming of the twelve stones on the breastplate after the tribes in Exodus 39:14 and their engraving as signets?
options: God personally acknowledges and identifies with each tribe
God treats the tribes as a single anonymous group
The tribes have no significance in God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: God personally acknowledges and identifies with each tribe
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:14 emphasizes the stones bear the names of the tribes like signet engravings, indicating God's personal covenantal acknowledgment of each tribe, affirming His intimate relationship with His people.

questions.question: How does the description of the tabernacle and its furnishings in Exodus 39:33-40 relate to the broader redemptive story of Scripture?
options: They prefigure Christ as the true meeting place between God and man
They symbolize human achievement without divine involvement
They depict a permanent earthly kingdom
They indicate the end of God's covenant
questions.correctAnswer: They prefigure Christ as the true meeting place between God and man
questions.explanation: The tabernacle and its furnishings (Exodus 39:33-40) typify Christ who fulfills the role of mediator and meeting place of God and humanity, connecting this chapter to the grand narrative of redemption.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the detailed priestly garments in Exodus 39 are merely ritualistic with no theological significance. What does Exodus 39:1-5 and 39:30 actually teach about the purpose of these garments?
options: They teach God's holiness and the necessity of consecration for mediation
They are purely decorative with no deeper meaning
They are designed for social status only
They were invented by humans without divine command
questions.correctAnswer: They teach God's holiness and the necessity of consecration for mediation
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:1-5 and 39:30 show the garments were made as the LORD commanded to reflect holiness and consecration, signifying the priest's role to mediate between God and Israel, thus affirming deep theological meaning.

questions.question: What synthesis of doctrines about God's glory and human mediation is seen in the making of the ephod and the breastplate with their respective materials and stones (Exodus 39:2 and 39:8-13)?
options: God's glory is manifested through the priest who mediates on behalf of Israel
God's glory is hidden and inaccessible
Human mediation is unnecessary in approaching God
questions.correctAnswer: God's glory is manifested through the priest who mediates on behalf of Israel
questions.explanation: The ephod (Exodus 39:2) and breastplate (39:8-13) with precious stones and colors signify God's glory, yet this glory is accessed through priestly mediation, combining doctrines of divine majesty and human representation.

questions.question: What theological significance does the inclusion of pomegranates and golden bells on the hem of the robe in Exodus 39:24-26 have in relation to worship and sanctification?
options: They symbolize fruitfulness and the audible presence of God in worship
They signify separation from the people
questions.correctAnswer: They symbolize fruitfulness and the audible presence of God in worship
questions.explanation: The pomegranates represent fruitfulness, and the golden bells indicate the audible presence of the priest in worship (Exodus 39:24-26), symbolizing sanctification and God's active presence in covenant worship.

questions.question: How does the completion of all the tabernacle work as commanded by God and verified by Moses in Exodus 39:42-43 connect to the doctrine of obedience and blessing?
options: Obedience to God's commands leads to His blessing
Obedience is irrelevant to God's favor
Blessing is independent of human action
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God's commands leads to His blessing
questions.explanation: Verses 42-43 illustrate that Israel's faithful obedience to God's commands resulted in Moses blessing them, affirming the biblical doctrine that blessing follows obedience to God's will.

questions.question: What synthesis of understanding about God's holiness and the role of the high priest is emphasized by the detailed descriptions of the priestly garments and the phrase 'HOLINESS TO THE LORD' (Exodus 39:29, 30)?
options: The garments and inscription emphasize God's holiness and the priest's consecrated mediatory role
The garments signify human authority over God
The inscription is a later addition with no original significance
The priesthood was a symbolic but meaningless ceremony
questions.correctAnswer: The garments and inscription emphasize God's holiness and the priest's consecrated mediatory role
questions.explanation: Exodus 39:29 and 30 together highlight that the high priest's garments and the inscription 'HOLINESS TO THE LORD' signify God's absolute holiness and the priest's sacred, mediatory function in approaching God.
